cells.tense: You are choosing a direction from where you stand, with your hand on the pen.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Take something you're already carrying and hold it at its honest size — no shrinking it to be polite, no inflating it to look like more. If someone presses you to make it smaller, leave it where it is.
cells.core:
You can point at something and mean it — this, not that — without bracing. The choice comes from where you are, not from what you're afraid of, and the ones nearby can feel the difference. You're not white-knuckling the outcome. You're standing where the direction gets picked, and picking.

Endurance is what this balance is free to feed next, and you already have some. Take something you're already carrying and hold it at the size it really is — no shrinking it to be polite, no inflating it to look like more. If someone presses you to make it smaller, leave it where it is. That's the whole ask. The direction stays clear because the load does.
cells.sheetLine: You can point at a thing and mean it, without bracing.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at what you choose
cells.place: at the fork where a direction is picked

cells.tense: You will be forcing an outcome that hasn't arrived yet, and calling it direction.
cells.act: see the whole pattern you are standing inside
cells.ask: Before pushing the next thing toward the outcome you've settled on, stop and look at the whole shape you're inside — the parts you planned and the parts you didn't.
cells.core:
Future-projected control is this same thing overdone. Direction stops being a choice and becomes a grip — steering tomorrow before tomorrow exists, reading the resistance as proof to push harder. From outside, the thing you're directing starts to look like it can't breathe. It'll do what you say, for a while.

Seeing the whole pattern is the way back, and you're built for it. Before pushing the next thing toward the outcome you've already settled on, stop and look at the whole shape you're inside — the parts you planned and the parts you didn't. Nothing has to be decided from there. Just see it at full size. The grip loosens when you see what you're actually holding.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing tomorrow before it has arrived.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at what you choose
cells.place: at the fork where a direction is picked

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that is already behind you, and you are still there.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Do today's next ordinary task the way you'd do it if nobody were watching, and don't explain the choice to anyone, including yourself.
cells.core:
The direction isn't gone; it's just not pointed anywhere. You're standing where the choice used to be, and the flatness has settled in. From inside, it doesn't feel like a decision not to pick. The door is behind you. You're still facing it.

Becoming what you already are doesn't have to be big to start. Do today's next ordinary task the way you'd do it if nobody were watching, and don't explain the choice to anyone, including yourself. Not to prove you can. Just because it's the way you do it. That one task, done your way, is the direction pointing again — and it was yours the whole time.

cells.tense: You are steering without watching your hands, through a stretch of life you keep writing.
cells.act: be what you already are, in your acts
cells.ask: Notice something you did today you'd call 'just how it goes' — then do that same thing tomorrow as a choice you're making on purpose.
cells.core:
You're directing. You just aren't the one noticing it. The momentum is real — your days move at a clip, the habit has a shape — but the habit is doing the picking, and asking you about it gets 'that's just how it goes.' Your hand is on it. You're not watching your hands.

Being what you already are is the way back, and it's the same line, earlier. Notice something you did today you'd call 'just how it goes' — the route you drove, the way you answered, the order you did things in — and do that same thing tomorrow as a choice you're making on purpose. Same act. Different footing under it. A few days of that and your hands are back in view.
cells.sheetLine: The momentum is real. Your hand is on the wheel.
cells.verb: pointing attention and energy at what you choose
cells.place: at the fork where a direction is picked
